## Findings and decisions

| Finding | Coordinator decision and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| **OD2-01: interaction intent** | **Accept, highest priority.** `nearestInteraction` uses body distance only; prompts and commands can select an off-screen or already-recorded clue. Use one authoritative target for prompt, visual cue and action, with view direction, reachable range and occlusion considered. Avoid nearest-object fallback behind the camera: that recreates the reported surprise. Looking deliberately at a known clue must still allow an informative notebook response; do not globally demote it regardless of aim. Target cues need to align with the real resource/evidence host and disappear when no valid target exists. |
| **OD2-02: Dart launch/return** | **Accept confusing launch/copy and missing impact feedback.** New Dart fabrication should face the proven clear launch lane, with accurate thrust/strafe/look labels and brief feedback for actual damaging impacts. Preserve the responsive acceleration/coasting baseline. Do not rotate parked legacy hulls or globally level saved pitch on boarding without a concrete camera/physics justification. Add a readable pitch/surface limit cue before changing orientation semantics. A hard speed gate must not strand a player in a failing craft; deliberate exit input is preferable to an unconditional speed lock. Keep safe-exit clearance and personal-depth rules. |
| **OD2-03: preparation/refit menus** | **Accept hierarchy, internal-ID exposure and repetitive/unnamed refusal problems.** Put actionable recipes and cargo first, collapse completed one-time work, retain repeatable recipes, preserve semantic focus and show descriptive cell/module labels. Distinguish carried materials from usable materials at the current site. The code already prefers a locker when no valid destination is remembered; the observed Dart destination can be retained selection. Fix context handling without silently overriding an intentional choice on every refresh. Crafting from the cradle is a gameplay-access decision, not a UI-only change; first clarify bench/cradle roles and make the route legible. Any later shared-workshop access must preserve restoration, locality and ingredient conservation. |
| **OD2-04: mouse-look continuity** | **Accept, high priority alongside interaction targeting.** Recommend captured look after a deliberate Play/Return/canvas gesture, with a visible drag-look alternative and remembered local preference. No capture on load, focus return or unattended Windows automation. Escape must release and pause; denied lock must leave a usable drag/keyboard path. Display sensitivity and complete control labels. Actual locked-motion and comfort need an isolated real-mouse/hardware check; the audit verified only lock entry/release and drag motion. No additional owner decision blocks recommending this conventional default. |
| **OD2-05: notice timing** | **Accept.** Code has one wall-clock toast slot with5.5/12-second expiry; it does not follow threat release. The inspected sheet retains warning text while the HUD says disengaging. Use event/state-aware transient notices and priority so successful save/export feedback does not obscure active danger. Preserve prominent persistence failures, unsaved-session warnings and graphics errors. Calm feedback must describe the current state rather than promise safety if a new threat starts. Exact new durations are trial values, not validated constants. |
| **OD2-06: creature visibility** | **Accept an approach-legibility concern; narrow the claim.** The sampled warning views do not show the hunter, but neither the frames nor this route establish that it is universally invisible. Earlier source-attributed views show its silhouette. The final-play C disable was deliberately caused by **terrain collision**, not a predator attack; it cannot substantiate invisible attack damage. Improve anticipation, readable wildlife presence on representative routes and off-screen direction without teleporting the animal into every camera view or exposing unseen creatures through geometry. Territory/warning tuning needs observed encounter comparisons. |
| **OD2-07: breathing/ascent clarity** | **Accept unclear near-surface breathing and blocked-rise feedback.** Show current breathing state and context-correct remaining suit/emergency air; preserve the simulation airway/depth authority. Avoid a generic auto-push through/around ceilings or automatic surfacing from every shallow position: it changes intentional hovering and may move players into hazards. First identify whether the observed rib cases are expected obstruction or collision traps, add understandable feedback/escape cues, and test any small geometry or movement adjustment with existing sweeps. A global buoyancy change is not an assumed low-impact UI fix. |
| **OD2-08: motion presentation** | **Accept pilot-specific guidance/pitch readability; defer speculative smoothing.** Sparse motion cues can be prototyped within richer cel. Fixed-step interpolation and input/render decoupling affect camera/optical/cockpit contracts; lack of interpolation alone does not prove bad high-refresh pacing. Measure on representative hardware before broad renderer changes. Extra inertia, shake and swim easing are not default improvements. |
| **OD2-09: first lead** | **Accept an interaction-host/value-hierarchy concern; learning remains a human-test question.** Bind the inspect affordance to the visible intake host and improve its local contrast before changing evidence location/range. Regional hints should remain physical and graduated without disclosing unknown coordinates. The single guided agent's six-minute search does not establish population difficulty. Canon/provenance-sensitive text remains protected from casual replacement. |
| **OD2-10: remaining copy/readability** | **Accept specific labels, grammar, contextual hints and contrast polish.** Coalesce bright-background guidance with existing ASTRA/SOL-M1-INTEGRATED-R1-01. Preserve deliberate keyboard-accessible opening skip rather than silently removing it; resolve any action/skip ambiguity with an explicit gesture and clear label. Keep reserve/pulse costs readily discoverable if contextualizing the persistent chip. |

## Recommended implementation order

The five priorities are **aimed interaction, reliable look/launch controls, concise preparation menus, timely encounter feedback, and readable breathing/navigation**. Preserve opening tone, collection feedback, bulk storage, useful trim tradeoffs, one-click service, notebook voice, the Dart's handling baseline and the improved richer-cel views.

Use two bounded sequential Sol6.1/max batches, each with exclusive ownership and the existing non-author Astra/Sol gate. These are proposed directions, not active assignments:

1. **Controls and action clarity.** One shared targeting rule/cue/prompt; deliberate captured-look entry/return with fallback; honest vehicle controls; new-fabrication launch heading and impact feedback. Prove a near-object choice, mouse/menu round trip, first launch/return and safe deliberate egress together. Specify any shared view/target/event interface before worker ownership. Do not combine automatic buoyancy, global pitch resets or renderer interpolation into this batch.
2. **Preparation and encounter flow.** Cargo/ready recipes first, compact contextual power/fit controls, descriptive identities and named refusals, state-aware warning release, secondary-text contrast, breathing-state/air-time display and local lead/obstruction cues. Re-evaluate one ordinary preparation→sortie→return/refit→next-outing sequence so fewer menu steps still support meaningful preparation. Add a targeted wildlife approach comparison; keep broader encounter/physics changes separately bounded if the evidence calls for them.

For launch validation, the old `dart-fabrication.json` has yaw0 and cannot prove a new-fabrication yaw change. Test a newly fabricated Dart through ordinary controls using a suitable pre-fabrication checkpoint, and separately verify the unchanged old save remains usable. For UI comparison, preserve actual starting state/viewport and count navigation, scrolling and refusals explicitly. An eight-action target is a hypothesis, not an acceptance number chosen to flatter a new layout.

Use a small set of purposeful before/after cases plus affected regressions, including persistent state/command safety, pointer-lock interruption, targeting occlusion and safe old-save use. No unchanged full art/carrier matrix or depletion run is needed absent a concrete affected risk. Functional changes invalidate affected acceptance and require the existing pair on the new frozen candidate. The later full-campaign Astra design critic remains scheduled.

After the control/flow changes, use the report's short fresh-human protocol: uncoached opening, take the Dart out and return, service/fabricate/fit/store, then respond to a warning. Record actual errors, hints, chosen controls, discomfort and understanding. Real mouse/audio/GPU checks complement model inspection; no fabricated enjoyment or duration pass.
